evidence: src/domain/ProjectRepository.ts, src/domain/TaskRepository.ts and src/domain/UserRepository.ts each declare a port with the same shape (save, findById), typed by its domain type: Project, Task or User.
src/domain/Task.ts: TaskEntity.markDone holds the only 'already done' invariant check, and assignToUser holds the assignment logic. Neither appears anywhere else in the module.
src/domain/TaskStatus.ts: the TaskStatus union and isValidTaskStatus both list the values 'todo' | 'in progress' | 'done'. This is a small duplication, but it stays within one file.
src/domain/TaskRepository.ts uses the TaskStatus type in findByProjectIdAndStatus instead of a raw string, so it does not bypass the type.

The entity styles differ: Project.ts has interface Project plus class ProjectEntity, Task.ts has abstract class Task plus TaskEntity, and User.ts has only interface User. This is a style inconsistency, not a split in concerns.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All seven files belong to one domain: projects, tasks and users. Each entity has its own repository port, and every port is written the same way. Each signature uses its file's own domain type (Project, Task, User, TaskStatus) and none uses raw shapes, so no file bypasses the module's abstractions.

Each rule or invariant lives in one place:
- The task lifecycle rule ("cannot mark done twice") appears only in TaskEntity.markDone.
- Assignment is handled only by TaskEntity.assignToUser.
- The set of allowed statuses is defined only in TaskStatus.ts.

There is one small duplication inside TaskStatus.ts. The status values appear in both the TaskStatus union type and the isValidTaskStatus guard. Because both are in the same file, this is a maintenance risk rather than a scattered invariant.

The entities are modelled in three different styles:
- Project is an interface plus ProjectEntity.
- Task is an abstract class plus TaskEntity.
- User is a plain interface.

This is a style inconsistency. It does not split the module into unrelated concerns, duplicate a rule across files, or bypass an abstraction, so it does not meet the Fail criteria. These observations lower confidence but do not cause a failure.
